Recent indicators point to continued solid real GDP growth. In standard New Keynesian/DSGE frameworks used by central banks, this implies a modestly positive output gap even as inflation—shown in the literature to be more persistent than real marginal cost via the Phillips curve—has moved closer to target. With unemployment up but still low, the 25 bp cut to a 4.25–4.50% funds-rate range is consistent with inflation-targeting practice and systematic interest-rate policy, while ongoing balance-sheet runoff keeps some restraint in place. Given the documented welfare costs of lingering inflation and the risk of inflation bias under discretion, the outlook is constructive but prudently balanced.
